sources.title: Palantir Form 10-Q for quarter ended June 30, 2026
Palantir Q2 2026 earnings release, Form 8-K Exhibit 99.1
Palantir and Microsoft Partner to Deliver Enhanced Analytics and AI Services to Classified Networks for Critical National Security Operations
sources.publisher: Microsoft Corporation and Palantir Technologies Inc.

claims.text: Palantir sells software that connects organizational data to operational decisions for commercial and government users. PLTR common stock is listed on Nasdaq in the 2026 quarterly filing.
Government and commercial are separate operating segments. Revenue is generally recognized across contract terms, so current revenue can lag changes in new sales or renewals.

evidence.locator: Item 7, Overview; risk factor on revenue recognized over contractual terms

claims.text: Foundry integrates data and workflows through the Ontology; AIP connects AI models to governed operations; Apollo delivers software updates; Gotham supports defense and intelligence missions.

Customers span government and commercial organizations. Government procurement and commercial deployment differ; multi-period contracts and termination provisions make contracted deal value an imperfect proxy for future recognized revenue.

evidence.locator: Item 1, Customers; Item 1A, government contracts and termination provisions

claims.text: AIP connects third-party, open-source, or self-hosted models with customer data and actions. Interpretation: Palantir sells operational integration and governance rather than being interchangeable with the underlying model suppliers.

Palantir identifies internal software development as a central alternative, alongside enterprise software vendors, government contractors, and systems integrators. The issuer does not provide a complete ranked competitor map.

Interpretation: an Ontology embedded in operational workflows can create switching costs. The claim depends on durable customer use and value; product descriptions alone cannot establish retention or pricing power.
On August 3 management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to USD 8,150–8,158 million. This forecast depends on continued deployment and expansion; it is neither earned revenue nor consensus.

For Q2 2026 ended June 30, GAAP revenue was USD 1,935.464 million, operating income USD 912.004 million, and net income attributable to common stockholders USD 1,061.890 million. Diluted GAAP EPS was USD 0.41. Common-stockholder net income differs from consolidated net income.

evidence.locator: Condensed Consolidated Statements of Operations, three months ended June 30, 2026

claims.text: At June 30, cash and equivalents were USD 2,030.047 million and marketable securities USD 7,379.052 million. Q2 GAAP stock-based compensation expense was USD 265.209 million. Interpretation: assess equity compensation and dilution alongside cash generation.

evidence.locator: Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets; Note 9, Stock-based Compensation Expense

claims.text: The August release identifies Alex Karp as CEO. The quarterly filing describes founder-controlled Class F voting rights subject to an ownership threshold; ordinary shareholders should distinguish economic ownership from voting influence.

evidence.locator: Note 8, Stockholders Equity / Class F common stock

valuation-context.unavailable: A current market price and forward consensus were not sourced. Any valuation must distinguish GAAP earnings, adjusted measures, and dilution; no current multiple or target is supplied.

claims.text: The August 3 outlook called for Q3 2026 revenue of USD 2,160–2,164 million. The next results will test that guidance; an independently verified release date was not retained in this packet.

Interpretation: long sales cycles, contract termination, deployment friction, and data or AI governance failures can impede growth. Repeated weak conversion of deals to durable production revenue would challenge the adoption thesis.

evidence.locator: Forward-Looking Statements, sales cycles, termination and deployment risks

claims.text: Bull: customers expand production use; base: deployment remains uneven; bear: internal alternatives or procurement constraints slow adoption. These are assumptions. Contract durability, customer-level economics, and the recurring role of investment gains remain open questions.

evidence.locator: MD&A, Overview / Results of Operations; Item 1A risks

claims.text: The 2024 Microsoft partnership pairs Palantir platforms with Azure government and classified environments. Classified availability was subject to authorization. This establishes an integration relationship, not exclusivity or proof that all announced deployments occurred.

August 3, 2026: Palantir reported Q2 results and raised full-year guidance. The August 4 quarterly filing supplies GAAP statements and updated risk disclosures; adjusted operating income and cash-flow measures require their separate reconciliations.

evidence.locator: Q2 Financial Summary; Outlook; non-GAAP reconciliations

gaps: Evidence cutoff 2026-10-18; latest financial statements reviewed cover 2026-06-30. SEC submission index was checked, but the issuer news site dynamically omitted article bodies on direct retrieval, so post-earnings news coverage is incomplete.
Current valuation, verified next earnings-release date, detailed customer concentration, and customer-level unit economics remain unsourced.
Liquidity amounts use all marketable securities in the balance sheet, not the narrower cash-plus-short-term-Treasury headline in the release.
Management forecasts and scenario assumptions are not realized results; no claim of independent verification of product superiority is made.
